sections.trivia:
There was no limited attendance for the game with police lifting the attendance bar of 30,000 which had stood for a number of games both at Celtic Park and Ibrox in response to past crowd trouble.
The weather was kind with a fine sky and warm for January.
sections.review:
Celtic led 1-0 at half time, Divers having scored in the 289th minute after Baxter had chosen to indulge in frills of ball control almost on his own penalty spot. An error by Haffey lsot Celtic the game. Scott sent over an ordinary high cross which Haffey missed completely allowing Wilson to head home. Byrne was the best winger even carrying a gashed ankle going into the game but he picked up a further injury in the 30th minute and became far less effective and pretty much a passenger for the rest of the game. It was a game of poor luck for Celtic with Chalmers missing a golden opportunity early, Conway having what appeared a good goal ruled ofut by Tiny Wharton and a Divers shot rolling along the goal line after coming off a post.
Commentators assured that though the victory went to Rangers, the honours went to Celtic.

sections.trivia:
On January 3rd, the whole Celtic team and Jimmy McGrory watched St Roch's fall to Cambuslang Rangers – the Junior 'Old Firm' tie. For St Roch's Jim Brogan who was booked to sign for Celtic in the coming season, scored twice. Also signed up was Benny Rooney from Petershill.
It emerged that Bertie Auld was in fact fit to play but was involved in transfer negotiations and therefore Celtic were loathe to play him. 
Alec Byrne had been to see a specialist to try and sort out the shoulder injury he sustained at Ibrox against Rangers in the previous game.
Billy McNeill was selected as captain for the Scotland U23 side to face the Second Division Select..
In came Charlie Gallacher for another game at outside right with Stevie Chalmers moving to inside left and Fernie moving to outside left.
The pitch was icy and the day gloomy with fog.
sections.review:
Celtic were twice ahead and twice pegged back by an injury-riven Third Lanark, and lost to a goal caused more or less by the icy conditions. Divers got the opener from a pass from Gallacher. Third Lanark almost immediately equalised when Haffey yet again pushed out a fairly innocuous looking cross directly to an opposition player and Harley scored. Celtic's second on 28 minutes was well crafted with Fernie and Peacock winning an opening for Divers to fire in a shot which could only be parried and Chalmers was the first to the rebound. As it began to snow Thirds came back again Hilley and Harley combining well for Harley to get his second.
Despite the snow neither team was ready to give up and both sides had good attempts in the second half. The winner came when Goodfellow was put through and he managed to slip the ball past McNeill then shoot against Haffey before prodding the rebound home with McNeill and Peacock in close attendance.

sections.trivia:
The English Football League came to an agreement with the Professional Footballers Association (Jimmy Hill was the chairman) so averting a football strike south of the border. The minimum wage was to be set at £15 per week for the First Division, £14 per week for the Second Division and £12 per week for the Third and Fourth. The maximum length of contract to be offered by a club was to be 2 years and the maximum wage limit was dropped.
John Hughes had recovered from his injury and came back in at centre forward at the expense of Jim Conway, who was in fact injured. Willie Fernie was also injured and Alec Byrne still recovering from his shoulder injury. The transfer negotiations to move on Bertie Auld looked to have fallen through enough that he was again included in the team.
The A Reserves played Aberdeen Reserves and were 3-0 up at half time. The team was Fallon, Donnelly, Jim Upton, Kurila, McNamee, Clark, Carroll, Jackson, Kelly, Don McMillan, Brogan.
Frost again and iron-hard ground conditions made it slippery under foot again for both teams./
sections.review:
Both sides had good chances in the first half with the goalkeepers having to be alert. Celtic opened the scoringwith a cleaver goal. Hughes took the ball out wide before slipping it to Gallacher in the centre who scored. Chalmers soon added a second with a neat gheader from a Divers lob.
Celtic had more chances to go further ahead at the start of the second half and on 66 minutes ther Dons pulled one back when Brownlie beat Haffey with a sharp shot. Divers completed the scoring when he cut in and shot. Ogston fumbled and Divers was there to knock home.

sections.trivia:
In a further move to beat the Professional Footballers Association call for a strike on 21st january, the Football League called on all clubs to rearrange their fixtures of the 21st to the Friday the 20th. Desp[ite appearing to have come to an agreement between the players and the League clubs, the League were determined to stave off the threat of a strike by the players to forego making drastic changes in the wage and contracft structure of players south of the border.
The tyeam sniffing around the transfer of Bertie Auld was Everton. Manager John carey had watched the previous game against Aberdeen. As yet they had tabled no firm offer but the bold bertie had been withdrawn from games before the Ne'erday game. Blackpool were also interested in signing the bold Bertie. They got as far as tabling a bid for £15,000 but in the end he did not want to leave. Fulham then made a late bid to take him south.
Alec Byrne again visited a specialist to check on the progress of his shopulder injury recovery. He picked up the injury against Rangers in the Ne'erday game.
Billy McNeill captained the Scotland U23 side against the Second Division Select at Brockville. The U23s won 10-2. Paddy Crerand was a non-playing reserve.
Charlie Tully handed in a transfer request to Cork Hibernian – then withdrew it, saying he would be happy to see out the rest of the season having reconsidered his position.
The only change to the side was John Clark coming in for Bertie Peacock, who had to withdraw with a boil on his leg. Duncan MacKay captained the side for the game.
The pitch for the game was well sanded and looked more like a beach.
sections.review:
Chalmers is credited with the initial goal in early reports.
Hughes had a shot cleared off the line in the first minuite and Chalmers a goal ruled out for offside in three. Divers got the first goal. Charlie Gallacher had probably his finest game to date with the accuracy of his passing and he made both the third and fourth goals for Chalmers and Crerand. Every one of the forwards had a decent game but Gallacher was a standout. behind the forwards the backs and half backs were so strong that they easily blotted out the Airdrie attacks with Kennedy and Clark being particularly effective. Airdrie were outclassed and only Leslie in goal prevented it from becoming a rout.

sections.trivia:
Finally Certic and Bertie made their minds up and declared that he was not up for sale, disappointing Nottingham Forest, Everton, Blackpool and Fulham.
Billy McNeill was picked for his first full Scotland cap against the Scottish League. Also selected was Duncan MacKay and Stevie Chalmers was a reserve. Pat Crerand was selected for the Scottish League with Jim Kennedy as a reserve.
Back in came Peacock with John Clark dropping out; and though Stevie Chalmers was out with 'flu, Willie Fernie was again fit and came in at inside left. Also back in training was Alec Byrne on the road to recovery from the shoulder injury which had kept him out since the turn of the year.
A number of crowd incidents were reported (see match report below) and led to arrests and appearances before the beaks on Monday morning. However it led the Evening Times inveterate bluenose journo Gair Henderson into a full blown rant about banner wavers on the Monday morning following the game. Incidents at games and crowd trouble had indeed been on the wane, particularly at Celtic – Rangers games so that this response from the bold Gair looked like jumping on the bandwagon.
sections.review: A fast and furious game packed with incidents. Celtic had to weather a full Falkirk storm at the start and did not gain any control till the own goal. Both defences played well and the difference lay in the quality of forwards and their skill, rather than their vigour which both sets showed to the full. Both Celtic penalties occurred when Fernie attempted to dribble through the maze of Falkirk defenders in the area and was tripped. Peacock converted both spot kicks. Falkirk had their own penalty on 69 minutes when Moran was fouled and McMillan beat Haffey. Falkirk's luck certainly wasn't in when Bertie Auld working in along the bye line after a short corner fired in a low and fast shot which took a deflection off of Thomson for an own goal. This was a decent cup tie in the spirit of cup ties with both sides giving everything.

sections.trivia:
Celtic were drawn at home to Montrose in the next round of the Cup.
Jim Conway handed in a transfer request. He had just managed a run of four games at centre forward for the first team with young John Hughes out injured and he looked the part after languishing in the Reserves. He clearly thought his chances of further first team action were limited in competition with Yogi and thought his prospects were better elsewhere. The club refused his transfer request.
An unchanged side for Celtic to the one that had beaten Falkirk in the Cup game the week before.
The pitch wore a light dusting of snow for the game and the weather was cold but fair.
sections.review:
A tricky surface to play on but Celtic started well with shots from Gallacher and Hughes. Celtic did most of the attacking and St Mirren packed their defense. Gradually the Buddies got back into it but just as they looked to have found their feet a Divers shot hit Wilson's arm to give Celtic a penalty. Peacock converted the spot kick to put the Bhoys in front. St Mirren pushed for an equaliser and on 50 minutes Kerrigan beat Haffey. Both sides pushed for a winner and in the last minute Bryceland darted through a scrum of defensers to score with a neat shot.
St Mirren maintained their unbeaten in '61 record.

sections.trivia: Stevie Chalmers had recovered from 'flu and started at inside left in place of Willie Fernie and Bertie was replaced by Alec Byrne.
sections.review:
It could not have been a more unfortunate start for Montrose. From a Gallacher corner Divers miscued the ball which cannoned off the foot of McCorquodale and behind for an own goal. Celtic then killed the game with goals in the 10th and 11th minutes from Hughes and Chalmers. A fourth followed and Hughes second from a mis-headed corner which still found it's way into the net. Divers injured a knee and went to outside right before leaving the field entirely and Celtic played the remainder of the first half and all the second with 10 men.
In the second half a fifth goal by Byrne was an individual effort beating three before shooting. Chalmers second and Celtic's sixth came when he headed home a Duncan MacKay cross.

sections.trivia:
Celtic were drawn against Raith Rovers away in the next round of the Scottish Cup
Billy McNeill was out with 'flu; into his position at centre half stepped John McNamee for his first team debut. Willie Fernie returned replacing John Divers who had strained knee ligaments in the previous cup tie against Montrose. Hibernian were undefeated in 11 games and were unchanged for the game.
Celtic A reserves played Hibs A Reserves. The team was Fallon, Donnelly, O'Neill, Kelly, Kurila, Clark, "Newman", Murdoch, Conway, McMillan, Auld. – the first appearance of Bobby Murdoch on a team sheet.
sections.review: Celtic started well and Hibs were quite lethargic. Celtic were two goals up in 16 minutes, both from Chalmers. McNamee played well at centre half and was little troubled by a Hibernian attack. Both Chalmers goals came from a neat crosses from Gallacher. The first headed home and the second five minutes later from a shot. All the Celtic forwards then proceeded to pepper the Hibs goal and only poor shooting and the uprights saved Hibs from being overwhelmed. Charlie Gallacher was becoming master of the right wing and had a great day.

sections.trivia:
Billy McNeill and Pat Crerand were selected for the Scotland U23 side to face England U23s on March 1. Frank Haffey was relegated to the bench with Ogston of Aberdeen coming in as goalkeeper. Jim Divers and John Hughes were also selected as reserves. Hughes in fact played when Ian St John was withdrawn by Motherwell to play in a Cup replay against Rangers, and John Divers withdrew with a knee injury.
There was pretty much a riot at Easter Road where Hibernian met Barcelona in the second leg of the Inter-City Fairs Cup quarter final. Hibs were awarded a penalty very close to the end, from which they scored to win 7-6 on aggregate.
Back in came Billy McNeill having recovered from 'flu. Out still was Jim Divers with strained knee ligaments and Bertie Auld was…… out in the cold with the Reserves.
sections.review:
Raith had two early escapes and looked to be on the ropes from the kick off. Chalmers got the first goal with a low shot into the corner of the net from a Hughes pass. A mix up between Mcneill and MacKay let Wallace in for Raith and he beat Haffey from 12 yards out. A minute later Leigh contrived to put the ball past his own keeper. fernie made it 3-1 with a great shot from 20 yards. Celtic had further chances but they went in at haldf time with the score 3-1 to Celtic.
Celtic were content to hold their lead in the second half and Raith presented little challenge to Haffey. Just before the final whistle Hughes headed a fourth.

The Scottish Second XI team to play a Junior Select side was announced and included Willie O'Neill (left back) and John McNamee (centre half). Bobby Carroll was a reserve.
A Monday night floodlit game and an unchanged side for Celtic. Clyde were wallowing in the depths of the division and flirting with relegation.
sections.review: John Hughes was the stand out of the win, scoring two, making one and generally combining well with Fernie and Chalmers. Clyde played well for the first 20 minutes and went ahead on 8 minutes when Robertson punished a defensive lapse. But by half time Celtic had pulled two goals back. Clyde also had Clinton injured in the first half. Gallacher scored a great goal in the second half. Clyde then proceeded to cave in and Chalmers and Hughes added 3 further goals.

sections.trivia:
Again an unchanged team for Celtic.
Ayr Utd were doing poorly in the First Division and sat rock bottom with 18 points from 26 games. However they had just come off of their first win in some time 
There were two 'bottle' throwing incidents occurred during the game firmly at the Celtic end. The first occurred at half time when a collection was being taken for Sea Scouts. One of the boys collecting was hit by a glass thrown from the Celtic end. The second was at the linesman who had been giving offside decisions against Celtic.
sections.review:
Celtic were keen to attack and Ayr to counterattack, but neither side appeared to have their shooting boots on correctly and a series of off-target shots resulted at both ends, none of which seriously troubled either keeper. The best of Celtic's lot was a shot from Chalmers which rebounded from the post and ran along the goal line to be cleared. On 41 minutes Fulton hit a 25 yard shot which Haffey failed to see through a mass of players. Celtic replied with gusto and Hughes very nearly levelled it before half time, his shot and rebound twice being saved by the Ayr keeper.
The equaliser finally arrived in the second half from a Chalmers shot which ballooned off the keeper and McNeill raced in to head the ball home. On 74 minutes Celtic went ahead from the penalty spot after Hughes had been upended in the box.. Hughes and McLean were booked late in the game and eight minutes from tiime Fernie added a third for Celtic.
All in all, pretty turgid stuff with the travelling support not doing itself any favours. A number of niggles and disputes took place between various opponents on the field and culminated in the two bookings. Fulton was injured for Ayr and in the second half played little part in the game after scoring.

sections.review:
Celtic were fancied by all to take this tie with ease. However Hibs had other ideas and it took till 5 minutes from the end to find an equaliser. Both goals came in the second half.
Celtic started very well and Simpson had to withstand a good deal of pressure in the opening minutes. Hibs defense appeared to be ably marshalled by Baird and after the opening flurry the Celtic forwards had trouble breaking through the line despite doing most of the attacking. John Hughes was getting little change out of Hibs centre half and was swapped with Alec Byrne.
Right at the start of the second half Kinloch scored for Hibernian and brought the attacking side of the Edinburgh club back to life. Celtic had to weather pressure for most of the second half till towards the end when they realised it was time to get after it. The equaliser came from a Billy McNeill clearance latched onto by Byrne who passed into the path of Chalmers to shoot home.
An escape for Celtic.

sections.trivia:
The draw for the semi-final was made with Celtic or Hibs facing Airdrie at home and Dunfermiline facing St Mirren at home.
Hibernian were unchanged for the replay. 
Celtic left naming their team till right before kick off. In came John Clark at left half for Bertie Peacock who withdrew with a knee injury.
The odds were against Hibernian as they had failed to beat Celtic in a Scottish Cup tie since 1902.
John Clark: “I  always say that I scored the best goal ever. It was in a Scottish Cup replay at Easter Road against  Hibs  [15th March 1961] and I beat a defender at the byline, cut in and  poked the ball through  [future Celtic keeper] Ronnie Simpson’s legs  and said to him: ‘You couldn’t get any better than  that could you!’”.  It was a vital goal in a 1-0 victory, although sadly we lost in the  final to Dunfermline that season.
sections.review:
Finally success for Celtic but it took till extra time to achieve the win.
The game was played at terrific speed and a credit to the fitness of the Celtic side was that they failed to wilt in extra time wheras the Hibs players all looked in need of a rest. Both Baxter and Byrne were booked during the game. Billy Mcneill had a terrific game at centre half with Baker only eluding him once in conventional time, Haffey coming to the rescue when the centre half slipped. The forwards wore down the Hibs defense with Fernie and Hughes in particular always testing. Hughes had a shot cleared off the line. As the game wore on Celtic gradually gained the upper hand and when it went to extra time there seemed to be only one possible outcome. John Clark got the winner with a shot through a melee of players from a cleverly worked short corner. The goal brought the supporters onto the field and it took some time before the game could continue to the final whistle.
Celtic would face Airdrie at Hampden in the semi-final.

sections.trivia:
An unchanged side for Celtic from the one that had beaten Hibernian in the Scottish Cup replay. John Clark retained his position at left half with Bertie Peacock still out with a knee injury.
In a trend seen this season towards a return to violent behaviour on the terraces, police were called into action in two games this weekend. The game between St Mirren and Airdrie at Love Street clashes required breaking up in the interval, and at this game at Firhill the police were in action immediately at the start of the second half when clashes broke out on the terracing.
Jim Conway broke his nose in a Reserve game and required an operation to reset it.
sections.review:
Celtic won a reprieve on 12 minutes after starting well. The Jags were awarded a penalty when MacKay handled a ball in the area. Wright took the spot kick which Haffey saved. Realising something better was required Celtic took the lead two minutes later. with Byrne heading home from a deep Gallacher cross to the far post. Celtic were now on top and looked the better side against a Partick team which were in the past a bogie team for Celtic. However Thistle were not finished and just before half time Joe McBride (who would go on to join Celtic) pulled a goal back. Back came Celtic and replied two minutes later when a neat pass from Hughes sent Chalmers in against the keeper with Stevie weaving the ball around Freebairn and into an empty net.
The restart was enlivened by fisticuffs and Glasgow's finest wading into the terraces. Onfield, Kennedy headed off the line and the Celtic goal received somewhat of an onslaught from the Maryhill Magyars – all to no avail. The score stood at 2-1 to the Celtic at the end and took the Bhoys up to 5th in the table

This was the game in hand that Celtic needed to play but its date presented somewhat of a problem for both sides in deiffering ways. Originally Raith Rovers did not want to play on this Monday night citing the closeness to the Saturday game. Celtic did not want to play on the Tuesday because this would have meant at least problems for Crerand and McNeill as they were selected to play for Scotland U23's on the Wednesday night. In the end Raith Rovers had to concede and the game went ahead on the Monday night.
Again an unchanged side for Celtic. Raith too were unchanged. Raith were involved in a relegation battle and every point for them was a step closer to surviving in the First Division.
sections.review: A very windy night with Celtic playing with the wind in the first half. Chalmers scored midway through the first half. MacKay missed a penalty for Celtic soon after, the Raith keeper making a decent save. Fox equalised for Raith in the second half.

sections.trivia:
On the 22nd, Billy McNeill and Pat Crerand played for Scotland U23s against England U23s at Ibrox winning 3-2.
Bertie Peacock passed a fitness test at Celtic Park before the game but was not used, instead he got some match fitness in playing with the reserves. The team here was unchanged with John Clark continuing at left half. Bertie's game for the reserves probably was too early and he suffered a recurrence of the injury.
sections.review:
Celtic started the game at a pace with Chalmers and Hughes going close. Dunfermiline weathered the opening storm and went on to score the opening goal on 19 minutes with a shot from Melrose from 20 yards which hit both posts before rolling in.Celtic had a claim for a penalty turned down soon after and the half ended with Dunfermiline attacking again having picked up their game from a lethargic start.
Celtic piled on the pressure at the start of the second and it paid off when Byrne danced past defenders and set up Fernie to shoot home. This was quickly followed by a second from Byrne himself with a wonder goal beating three defenders before prodding the ball past Connachan. Byrne had the beating of the Dunfermiline defenders in the second half but his crosses and passing failed to add to the score.

sections.trivia:
Celtic were still concerned with Bertie Peacock's leg / knee injury which he had aggravated playing in a Reserves game on the previous Saturday. John Clark had ably deputised at left half for the injured Bertie for the last four first team games. In the end both sides fielded unchanged sides from the previous week.
Played at Hampden Park with a 3:00 pm kick off.
In the other semi-final Dunfermiline and St Mirren played out a 0-0 draw at Tynecastle. Dunfermiline played with 10 men when their centre forward Dickson was stretchered off.
Ex-Celt Jim Sharkey was in the Airdrie side. He moved on to Raith Rovers in May 1961 after being accused of going easy against Celtic in this Scottish Cup semi-final defeat.
sections.review:
A contest for twenty minutes during which time Haffey made two fine saves from Storrie. Celtic's first attack saw a fine move starting with Crerand to Gallacher to Hughes , whose shot hit centre half Johnstone on the head and laid him out!.The first corner came on 14 minutes and flew well over. There were wild shots from Gallacher and Chalmers but on 19 minutes Fernie passed to Byrne who beat his man and sent over a cross which Hughes headed powerfully past Leslie. The goal served to emphasise Celtic's forward superiority and steadfastness of their defense. Airdrie seemed cowed by the loss of the goal and the second soon followed. Byrne cut the ball back to Fernie and though his shot was saved Hughes was on hand to tap home the rebound.
Sharkey roused himself and hit a good shot which Haffey had to dive across goal to save. The third goal came from a classic move between Gallacher and Chalmers. As Chalmers raced through the centre, Gallacher anticipated his position and sent a wonderful pass through which Stevie raced on to completely deceive Leslie by chipping the ball over him and into the net. Back time and again came Celtic and they might have scored thrice more before Fernie wandered in from the right and completely fooled Leslie with a flick from the outside of his boot.
Four-nil to the good at half time, Airdrie were down and out. Celtic continued to dominate the second half but the urgency had gone. Hughes had the ball in the net again only to be ruled offside. Crerand and Gallacher passed meticulously. A the defense were rarely beaten.

sections.review:
A rain soaked game which no doubt kept the numbers attending down.
Perhaps tyhe rain affected the game but the Celtic forwards fauiled tyo find the rhythm that had set them uop so well against SAirdrie. They had the majority opf the play but failed to gel in the same way and were profligate in front of goal. Hughes, Fernie and Chalmers all missed simple chances. St Johnstone took the lead with a low shot that beat Haffey. fernie equalised direct from a corner when his corner hit the underside of the bar and Taylo in attempting to punch it clear only managed to palm it into the net.

sections.trivia:
A Monday afternoon game with Celtic staying in Arbroath after the Saturday game against Dundee. Celtic fielded an unchanged side.
Though Bertie Peacock did not play he still had an important role. He went to see Airdrie take ion Dunfermiline and two nights later also went to see Clyde hand out a 6-0 defeat of Dunfermiline.
Frank Haffey and Billy McNeill were in the Scotland side beaten 9-3 by England at Wembley on 15th April. Such was the effect on Frank that John Fallon expected to take his place in the Celtic team to play Dunfermiline in the Scottish Cup Final.
Yuri Gagarin became the first man into space on 12th April.
sections.review:
Dundee United's goal came when Mochan danced through a group of players and unleashed a 20 yarder which Haffey palmed out only to see Ormond latch onto the replay and score. This was after Celtic had had the better of the opening. With just eight minutes remaining Gallacher sent over a cross that the United defense left and GHughes headed home an equaliser.
Once more the team was wasteful in front of goal with Fernie and Chalmers working good openings but shots going astray.

sections.trivia:
Celtic received a scare when the Scotland players reported back from the debacle at Wembley and Billy McNeill reported a back strain. McNeill had missed very few games for Celtic this season with McNamee deputising before when he was on international duty, and John Kurila coming in during late August / September when Billy was out injured. The injury turned out to be not as serious as first thought and after a day McNeill returned to training.
The other poser for Celtic was whether to play Bertie Peacock or the young John Clark at left half. Bertie was again fit and ready to play, having come through a Reserve match on the Wednesday night against Ayr Utd reserves. John Clark had more than ably deputised for the Celtic captain since Bertie had picked up his injury.
For Dunfermiline, their experienced outside right Tommy McDonald failed to make the team when he was taken to hospital with appendicitis. Peebles moved across to the right and in came youngster Dan McAlindon.
On the world stage, USA and President Kennedy supported the invasion of Cuba at the 'Bay of Pigs'. The invading forces were entirely defeated by Castro's army
sections.review:
This was Dunfermiline's first appearance in a Cup Final and the  Hoops had failed to win the trophy since 1953/54. Dunfermiline were of  course managed by a certain John Stein. Jock had taken over the previous  year at East End Park but had a very good knowledge of the Celtic team having coached many of them when he was Reserve Trainer and Coach at Celtic Park before leaving for Dunfermiline.
A thoroughly entertaining game which saw both sides have chances and both defenses perform well. Part Crerand had the stand-out game for Celtic supplying accurate pass after accurate pass.
The game ended goalless and both goalkeepers  came in for praise., Frank Haffey pulling off a great save late in the  game to deny the Pars – who were down to 10 men after centre-half  Williamson went off injured..
The replay was four days later.

sections.trivia:
Following the disappointment of being the losing finalist in a replayed Scottish Cup, Celtic returned to playing out the rest of the season – the main importance being whether they finished third or fourth in the League.
After playing for the best part of four months with the Reserves, Bertie Auld was again the centre of transfer rumours. He had been watched in the Reserve League decider against Hearts by representatives from Birmingham City and a bid was expected. Bertie had refused to move to Blackpool in January even though a fee had been agreed between the two clubs. Despite Celtic always saying that they would never transfer a player that did not want to leave, there is without doubt the feeling that Bertuie had been demoted to the Reserves (losing his place in the first team to Alec Byrne) for failing to agree to Celtic's wish to transfer him for a fee to Blackpool. Bertie duly was transferred to Birmingham on the 1st May for a fee estimated to be around £15,000.
In a day of busy business Jim Conway was also transferred to Norwich City for a fee of £12,000.
Charlie Gallacher appeared to take the rap for the Cup Final replay loss and was dropped in favour of Stevie Chalmers moving to outside right and Bobby Carroll coming into the team at inside right.
South of the border, Bobby Evans was freed from Chelsea after 1 season at the club.
Rangers duly won the Scottish League with a 7-3 win over Ayr Utd (who were relegated along with Clyde)
sections.review:
Celtic escaped an early scare when O'Neill cleared off the line. Motherwell were the better team at the start and scored first with Roberts beating Haffey with a shot on 5 minutes. Celtic equalised with a neat move from Hughes, Carroll with Chalmers finishing. A period of Celtic pressure followed without producing a goal. Roberts put Motherwell aghead just before the interval.
Motherwell came out better in the second half and were unlucky not to further increase their lead. Five minutes before the end Fernie equalised for Celtic with a shot from the edge of the area.

Two Celtic players were transferred on the 1st May. Bertie Auld was given a transfer to Birmingham City after the clubs agreed a fee of around £15,000. Jim Conway was also transferred to Norwich City for a fee of £12,000.
Crerand and McNeill, who would be playing for Scotland the following night, were rested. In came John McNamee and Johnny Kelly. Also out was Alec Byrne and in a reshuffle of the front line, in came John Divers for his first start since the end of January. For Queens, W Neil at centre half joined from Airdrie only a few hours before kick off.
sections.review:
Once again Celtic came up against a goalkeeper on excellent form. Despite having the majority of the play, they found Donaldson leaping like a cat to make spectacular saves, even stopping a MacKay penalty in the first five minutes. McNamee in conceding the free kick that led to Queens third goal injured himself and Celtic played the last ten minutes with ten men. After drawing 3-3 the tie went to Celtic on the toss of a coin.
Celtic would meet Clyde in the final.
